learning_outcomes.text: Introduce the principal models, methods, and tools for managing and organizing firms.
Enable students to comprehend the particular contexts they encounter and also to recognize, articulate, and address challenges.
Analyze balance sheets and make decisions typical of the contexts in which companies operate (e.g., capital budgeting analysis, make or buy decisions, etc.).
Develop technical skills for balance sheet analysis.
Enhance teamwork, report writing, and presentation abilities within a set timeframe through the optional project.
Gain or enhance awareness of economic and business issues.

syllabus_topics: Work division and coordination; job design; organizational design, main organizational models.
Accounting model and the role of external accounting
Cost analysis in the long term: economies of scale, scope and learning
Short term decisions: break even, mix and make or buy.
assessment_rules: The assessment includes a verbal examination, which is conducted after one or two written assignments that may be reviewed during the oral segment. A mid-term test will be proposed in the last weeks of the course, which, if passed, can be used instead of the exercises proposed at the beginning of the exam session. There is an optional project where participation can be considered as part of the total exam evaluation. To pass the exam, comprehension of the complete syllabus is necessary, except for the section addressed by the optional project (balance sheets and analysis of balance sheets). The exam is graded out of thirty.
